findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the Certified Food Manager Certificate (CFM) on file to have expired in March of last year. The person in charge (PIC) stated that they have not retaken the test since then. Inspector provided PIC with a handout on accredited institutes through which they may retake the exam. A CFM must be on site at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM helps to oversee proper food handling and cold holding temperatures to ensure facility is in compliance with safe food handling and preparation. Retake the test by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 
During today’s visit inspectors observed multiple items in the hand sink. PIC was made aware and Items were removed. Ensure that the hand sink is available for hand washing at all times. 

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed mouse dropping next to a bag of wheat flour in the facility’s dry storage area. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned the area immediately. Ensure the facility is cleaned on a routine basis to eliminate conditions for pest harborage.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11(A) 
Multiple cardboard boxes of food items were observed store directly on the floor in different areas in the facility. PIC was informed. PIC assured inspectors that the boxes will be removed from the floor. Ensure that food items stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from form splash, dust, or other contamination.

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
6-101.11(A)
Inspectors observed ice accumulation in multiple Chest sliding freezer. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated Ice accumulation will be clean. Ensure that Ice is cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated inspected that training will be done soon. Ensure all workers who handle or prepare food have and maintain their Food Handler’s Certificate every 3 years. Food Handler’s must have a certificate on file within 30 days of hire. Ensure these documents are available upon request during future inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple items (pork belly, Mackerel, Tilapia) to have torn packaging, or be outside of their packaging in the sliding chest coolers & freezers. CORRECTED- items were re-wrapped. Ensure all temperature control for safety (TCS) food items that are packaged on site retain their seal to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the sliding chest cooler in front of the food prep area to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the PIC added an ambient thermometer to the cooling unit. Ensure all cooling units contain an ambient thermometer to measure the temperature at the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility ensure all cooling units are working properly to hold items at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: 1) Inspectors observed mouse droppings on the floor and between boxes in the back dry storage area (shipping container). 
2) Inspector also observed a dead bug on a noodle package on the top shelf of the open air cooler. CORRECTED- this item was removed from service by the PIC.

The facility uses Sonny Adams for Pest Control once monthly. Droppings should be cleaned up, but large pallets of food will need to be moved to properly clean. Contact pest control operator, and monitor the area for evidence of pest after clean up, and check shipments for pests during delivery.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of brown rice being stored in a cardboard box, with an open top in the back dry storage area. Foods in dry storage should be completely covered in a food-grade package or container to prevent the contamination of food. This storage method also may attract pests (see violation #38). Ensure foods are protected from contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

See that hot water is always available. A new hot water heater was just installed and hot water was able to be supplied during the inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Quail eggs were observed in a double door cooler above kimchi and other packaged items. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged to keep quail eggs below packaged foods. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st  REPEAT: No ambient thermometer is present in the 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC added a thermometer to the cooler. 
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. [C]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
Repackaged frozen meats observed in two chest freezers without appropriate labeling. The facility has been able to properly label multiple foods, there remains some whole, intact fish that need proper cooking instructions (the common name is indicated on the freezer holding the foods. See that cooking instructions are available either on the packaging OR simply print a label to affix to the front of the freezer.  

3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD/identity statement; 106 (2) List ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, declaration of artificial colors and flavors and chemical preservatives; (3) net contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (5) MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS. (6) Nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling UNLESS EXEMPT Under FDCA. (Pf) (C) Bulk FOOD for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be labeled in plain view. (D) Bulk, unPACKAGED FOODS portioned for CONSUMERS shall be properly labeled. [C]

There are still a very small number of mouse droppings observed in the far back storage area. Droppings are minimal and may be easily cleaned BUT pallets of bulk foods will need to be moved in-order to properly clean. Continue to provide regular PCO service and monitor and clean when activity is observed.  No damaged packaging is observed. 

The facility will be given thirty days to inspect to allow ample time for proper cleaning. 
PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.comment:
4-303.11: There is no bleach available within the store. The facility does minimal processing and does not immediately need the sanitizer. See that bleach is provided and that the available test strips are used to determine the proper concentration (100-200ppm).

(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: There is pressed wood shelving over the triple sink that is unsealed. Properly seal/paint the shelves so the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Also, a couple of the reach-in freezers are observed to have significant ice accumulation. Defrost the freezers so they are able to be easily cleaned. 
Also, there is cardboard being used on the top of a roll cart adjacent to the wrapping station. See that the cardboard is removed and replaced with a cleanable surfaces (think plastic sheet). The cardboard is protecting over single-service items. The cardboard is starting to show signs of wear and should be replaced with a suitable alternative.  

(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
4-101.16:  The facility is using sponges to wash, rinse, and sanitize utensils. Cease use of sponges and switch to a cloth that can be properly laundered between uses. Facility was educated on proper ware washing and use of materials for the task. Demonstrated use of bleach and test strips too. Facility truly only uses a small amount of equipment for cutting of fruits and meat. Discussed washing-in-place of the saw blade. 
Sponges may not be used in contact with cleaned and SANITIZED or in-use FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. [C]

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
There is no garbage can present at the prep area handwashing sink. Provide a trash can for disposal of paper towels.
5-501.16: (C) A waste receptacle shall be located at each lavatory if disposable towels are used. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner took food manager course through SCDPH in March 2020 but does not have a copy of certification. Owner was advised on process to obtain a copy of the CFM certificate (see general comments for details). 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Wood was painted at the partition installed at the meat packing area. Gaps remain to be sealed along edges of wood and plastic covering on the outside along the aisle. 
-Ceiling of the entryway and the area outside the building where the metal carton and the building meet have not yet been repaired to eliminate entrance of rainwater into the building. It was not raining at the time of inspection, so leaking rainwater was not an issue. Owner was advised to get the necessary repairs completed to minimize leaking rainwater during future weather events. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Owner has not yet obtained a food manager certification, and several priority violations were observed at the time of inspection. Priority violations included, but were not limited to, a retail cooler knowingly holding above 45F used for storage of TCS foods, lack of handwashing in the meat packaging area, lack of ware washing for food contact surfaces, and proper bleach was not available for use.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner does not have a food manager certification. Owner noted a food manager course and exam were completed through SCDPH in 2019, but owner never received results or the certification. Owner was provided with information to contact ServSafe to follow-up on certification.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Owner could not locate employee health policy documents provided and discussed during previous routine inspection. Copies of signed reporting agreements were not available for the owner and his staff. Revised versions of employee health documents were provided on new letterhead with updated reference to 2017 FDA Food Code and discussed. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for all staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure with specific actions to be taken in case of a vomit and/or diarrhea incident was not available. Norovirus disinfection handout was provided and discussed. Bleach is available for use. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy on-site along with all other employee health documentation.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Handwashing could not occur at meat packaging area as needed between tasks because the handwashing sink was blocked. Proper handwashing between tasks and ensuring access to allow proper handwashing were discussed. An employee was later observed washing hands at the designated handwashing sink when it was accessible. 
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Upon arrival handwashing sink in packaging area was blocked. Foam trays were observed in the basin, and trays with meat that were waiting to be wrapped were balanced along the edge of the handwashing sink. Employee working in the area was advised on proper use of the handwashing sink. All items were removed to allow for access to the handwashing sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin and along the outer edge of the handsink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Cartons of raw quail eggs were stored above cheese and bread in a retail cooler. Proper storage of raw animal foods was discussed. Eggs were discarded due to improper holding temperature (see #22 & 33 for details).
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 While discussing the cleaning procedure for the meat saw, owner stated the saw is cleaned at the end of the day using only hot water. Owner was advised that all food contact surfaces (any surface that food comes in contact with during use) must be manually washed with hot soapy water, rinsed with clean water, and then sanitized with a bleach solution. Owner stated he understood and moving forward the meat saw would be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized between uses. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 A proper sanitizer was not available for use. Lemon scented bleach and an unopened ammonia chloride disinfectant were observed in the meat packaging area. Bleach was purchased during inspection. Ensure proper sanitization of all food contact surfaces. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 TCS foods in the 2 door retail cooler had internal temperatures at 46F-52F. Foods included yogurt (48.5F), multiple packages of tofu (46.5F-51.5F), soy puffs (50F), and quail eggs (52F). Foods in question were discarded in the dumpster during inspection. Photos were taken, and a voluntary order of destruction was generated.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 A small bottle of lemon scented bleach was observed in the meat packaging area. Proper use of approved sanitizers was discussed. No more cutting or packaging of products could occur until proper bleach was provided. Bleach was purchased during the inspection. Owner was advised to maintain all bleach solutions at 200ppm as required by the product label directions.
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Two door retail cooler was holding above 45F. Digital thermostat was observed at 46F. Inspector placed thermometers in the cooler and observed temperatures at 48F-50F. Owner noted the cooler digital thermostat was reading at 46F for the last couple of weeks and that service was needed. All TCS foods were discarded during inspection (see #22 for details). Owner put a call in for service. Owner was advised the cooler cold not be used for storage of any TCS food until it is able to maintain foods at 41F/below. Owner stated he understood. 
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Boxes of frozen fish that needed to be separated and portioned prior to being placed in retail freezers were sitting on the floor at room temperate. Owner noted the fish was previously stored in the walk-in freezer but removed to allow fish to thaw slightly so products could be easily separated during portioning. Proper thawing was discussed, and boxes of fish were placed in the walk-in cooler.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.14 Fly strip was observed hanging in the middle of the meat packaging area. Fly strip was removed and discarded at request of inspector. Owner was advised on proper placement of fly strips in the future. Ensure fly strips are not placed directly above meat packaging. 
Unpackaged food shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination during prep.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bags of onions were on the floor in the walkin cooler. Several boxes of produce and other foods were also observed on the floor in the walk-in cooler and in the store. Proper storage at least 6 inches off the floor was discussed.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Freezer used for storage of banana leaves and other items had heavy ice buildup, and old, damaged cardboard boxes used as partitions between foods. Defrost the freezer and remove old cardboard. Cease the practice of using cardboard in freezers and provide additional hard plastic dividers similar to those observed in other freezers. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for use in meat packaging area while employee was working. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared and available for use when working in the meat packaging area. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 Rain water was leaking in at the entryway between the store and the back storage area. Metal containers were used to catch dripping water. Get the ceiling of the entryway and the area outside the building where the metal carton and the building meet repaired to eliminate entrance of rainwater into the building. 
-A new partition with wood and plexiglass has been installed at the meat packing area. Raw wood needs to be painted, and all gaps between wood need to be sealed with caulk.
-WALK-IN FREEZER - 1. Piece of wood at the threshold was loose. Seal the wood to the floor. 2. Foam insulation was exposed around the doorframe inside the walkin freezer. Seal the inner doorframe of the walk-in freezer. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner needs to take a food manager course to obtain a food manager certification.
See general comments for details.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Package of moldy oyster mushrooms was observed in the refrigerated display case. Mushrooms were removed to be discarded.
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bags of onions were on the floor in the walkin cooler.
--Boxes of foods were on the floor in the walkin freezer.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Handle of scoop for unshelled peanuts was observed touching food product. Owner was advised to provide a storage container that can hang over the outer edge, such as a plastic pitcher, to promote proper storage of scoop between uses.
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Foam food trays used for portioning bulk meats were soiled with debris accumulation. Soiled trays were discarded, and remaining trays were inverted to protect food contact surfaces from potential contamination.
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Cardboard remained on the metal table that had a deteriorated surface underneath. Options for replacing the table and/or providing a cleanable surface, such as treated/painted wood, were discussed.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Owner/PIC at time of inspection does not have a food manager certification. Manager certification for another employee was available, but the designated PIC must be a CFM (see general comments for details).
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Based on the conditions observed at the packaging area and in the restroom, staff have not been washing their hands (see #10 for details). Handwashing at designated handsinks between tasks with proper technique was discussed with the owner.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Upon arrival handsink in packaging area was blocked with soiled wiping cloths and foam food trays. All items were removed from the sink. Proper use of handsink and accessibility were discussed. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of placing items in the basin of the handsink for any reason. 

6-301.11 Hand soap bottle was empty in the restroom. Soap at the handsink in the packaging area was watered down. Dish soap was at the far end of the 3 part sink and provided for inspector to wash hands. Maintain soap that is not watered down at both handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not located at the handsink in the packaging area. Paper towels were observed at the right drain board of the 3 part sink. Owner was advised the current location did not promote proper handwashing. Provide a paper towel dispenser and place paper towels at the handsink in the packaging area. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Packages with moldy Shitaki mushrooms were observed in the refrigerated display cooler. All portions were removed to be discarded. 
Sliced winter melon in the walkin cooler was without a date mark and observed to be spoiled. Winter melon was removed to be discarded.
Boxes with moldy peanuts in shells were observed up by the drink cooler in the front of the store. Peanuts were said to be set aside for discard. Owner removed peanuts from the front service area. 
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 & 4-702.11 Cutting board and cleaver used the evening prior for cutting and portioning raw shrimp were soiled with food debris. Also, plastic tubs, bowls, pots, and trays were observed on the floor under the 3 part sink. 
Equipment was not cleaned and sanitized after use. Owner was advised on proper ware washing of all food contact surfaces between uses. Poster showing setup for proper manual ware washing was available for reference on the wall above the 3 part sink.
--Later an employee was observed placing the cleaver in a drawer after it was washed and rinsed. The sinks were not setup, and the cleaver was not exposed to proper sanitization. Proper ware washing was discussed. 
Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned after use and sanitized before use after cleaning.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach available for use did not have an EPA registration number on the label. Owner stated he would obtain proper bleach for use later that day. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Bags of coconuts and shelled peanuts were observed on the floor in the walkin cooler. Foods were placed on shelving during inspection.
--Boxes of foods were all over the floor in the walkin freezer. Owner was advised to provide a means to elevate the foods in the walkin freezer at least 6 inches off the floor.
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Handle of scoop for unshelled peanuts was observed touching the food product. Owner repositioned the peanut scoop so the handle was up out of the peanuts. Owner was advised to consider getting some sort of holder for the scoop to encourage proper storage outside of the peanuts between uses. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Foam food trays used for portioning bulk meats were observed to be soiled with debris accumulation in the packaging area. Some of the trays were initially observed with soiled wiping cloths in the basin of the handsink. All trays in question were discarded during inspection. 
Single service and single use articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.16 Soiled cardboard was observed under the cutting board at the 3 part sink in the packaging area. Cardboard was discarded.
--Soiled cardboard and sections of a liner with a foam backing were observed lining the small metal shelves in the packaging area. Remove soiled cardboard and liners with foam backing. Provide a cleanable surface for lining the shelves. 
--Soiled cardboard was observed lining the top of a metal table that had a deteriorated surface underneath. Owner was advised to cease the practice of using cardboard. Clean and remove damaged surface on the top of the metal table, and provide a cover that is cleanable.
--Heavy ice/frost accumulation was observed along the top inside the doors of the freezer holding eggrolls. Owner was advised to defrost the freezer and maintain it in a manner that is easy to clean. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-501.14 The 3 part sink was observed to be heavily soiled with food and general debris in all three compartments. It did not appear the 3 part sink was used for ware washing any time recently. All of the compartments and the drain board needed to be cleaned. Cleaning began during inspection. 
Clean the sinks and drain board at the 3 part sink daily/as needed and between uses and maintain them clean. 
The compartments of sinks, basins, or other receptacles used for washing and rinsing equipment and utensils shall be cleaned: (A) before use, (B) throughout the day at a frequency necessary to prevent recontamination of equipment and utensils and to ensure that the equipment performs its intended function; and (C) if used, at least every 24 hours.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following items were soiled:
1) walkin cooler shelving (dust/mold); 
2) refrigerated display cooler holding eggs (general buildup/dust); and
3) packaging area - general surfaces of shelving and table holding wrap station (splash/debris).
Clean the aforementioned items and all general surfaces daily/as needed, and maintain them clean. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Puddle of dirty waste water was observed in the mop bucket. Waste water was discarded and mop bucket cleaned during inspection. 
All sewage and waste water must be routed to an approved sewage disposal system. Properly dispose of mop water after use and do not leave it sitting in the facility.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Handsinks were observed to be soiled, especially the restroom handsink which had grimy buildup. Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed and maintain them clean. 
--Walkin cooler floor was soiled with buildup under shelving, and dust was starting to buildup on the ceiling above the fan. Clean the ceiling and the floor in the walkin cooler.
--Ceiling was damaged and falling down at the doorway between the dry storage area and the store. 
A few ceiling tiles in store were also observed with severe water damage. Owner noted repairs are needed for the roof. Provide repairs and replace the damaged tiles and ceiling in the aforementioned area.  
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-303.11 Lighting in the restroom was very dim, and one bulb was flickering. A flashlight was needed to see general surfaces clearly. Repair/replace lighting in the restroom. 
Light intensity shall be at least 20 foot candles (215 lux) in restrooms.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. Worker present at the time of inspection confirmed he did not have a certification. Employee was advised as to online course options for earning certification. 
All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Several peanuts in the fresh peanut box were observed to be moldy. Go through peanuts daily and throw away any that are not in sound condition. A new bag of peanuts was purchased and set out for sale at the store. 

Two balut eggs were observed to be cracked and damaged. One egg had what appeared to be solidified black liquid on the outside. Both eggs were discarded at the time of inspection.

Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text:
750.240 - Frozen chicken paws, whole duck, and pork stomach were sitting out on a table in the back retail area. Items were still fairly frozen, and surface temperature of duck was 32°F. Owner stated the products were in the walkin cooler overnight and placed out at ambient temperature around 10a. All products were placed back in the walkin cooler.

Also, wonton wraps that were labeled keep frozen or refrigerated were observed sitting out at the front of the store. Owner noted the product was purchased by a local restaurant but he had not yet had time to deliver it. Wonton wraps were placed back in cold holding until they could be delivered.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.
Cease the practice of sitting frozen foods at ambient temperature. Leave items in cold holding until they are intended to be used and are properly thawed.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 130 -  Raw meats (beef, pig head, and whole duck) were stored over and next to kenkey (cooked product), vegetables, and noodles in the walkin cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage. 

Scoop used with fresh peanuts still in the shell was heavily soiled with buildup. Clean and sanitize the scoop daily.

Half bowl that appeared to be the packaging for a product was observed as the scoop for unshelled peanuts. Bowl was removed. Owner was advised to obtain and use a proper scoop with a handle for the unshelled peanuts. 

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times. Use proper scoops; clean and sanitize scoops daily. 
 All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
(R) 750.120 - Several boxes of various products were observed on the floor. 

Food shall be protected at all times and stored at least 6 inches off the floor. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Handsink in packaging area was clearly not being used for handwashing. The sink was dry, had a knife sharpening stone in the basin, and no paper towels were available. The sink was also blocked (see #31).  Paper towels were provided, and the sharpening stone was removed from the basin.

Employees must wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A rusty cleaver and a rusty knife were observed in the packaging area. Owner and employee working in the area stated the cutlery in question was not used. Remove the rusty cutting utensils from the store.

Plywood was observed covering the middle basin and part of the right basin at the 3 part sink. The wood in question was splintered and had some pieces missing. The plywood is used as a surface for packaging and cutting fish when needed. Employee working in the area noted another material is placed on top of the plywood. 
Remove the plywood and replace it with a proper food grade material such as a sturdy cutting board.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Three part sink is not being properly used for ware washing. Use the 3 part sink as intended for manual wash, rinse, and sanitize of food contact surfaces.

For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Chlorine test strips were not available for checking sanitizer concentration. Obtain and use chlorine test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - No sanitizer of any kind was available for use at the facility during the inspection. Bleach was purchased and brought to the facility during the inspection. (see general comments for additional information)

Employee in packaging area was asked about sanitizer and whether bleach has been used in the past for sanitizing dishes. The cleaver used for chopping was said to only be cleaned with soap and water. Food contact surfaces are not being properly cleaned and sanitized.

Soiled scoop used in fresh peanuts was cleaned with soap and water but was not sanitized in bleach solution. Proper wash, rinse, and sanitize process was discussed.

To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.
Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Handsink in packaging area was blocked by wire shelving being used for storage. Several items were stacked on the top shelf inhibiting access to the handsink.  Items were removed from the to shelf to allow for partial access, and hands could be washed. The area needs to be rearranged and the shelving in question completely relocated so this issue does not have the potential to happen again. The shelving is barely a couple feet away from the front of the handsink.

Handsinks are to be accessible at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Restroom door has a self-closer, but the door does not shut properly. Adjust the self-closer to allow the restroom door to shut properly.

Also, the restroom was in general dirty. Clean the restroom daily/as needed, and maintain it clean. 

All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 - Floor to wall juncture beneath packaging area handsink and around the walkin freezer door are not properly sealed. Seal the area where the floor and the wall meet in these areas.

The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.1210 & 1220 - A) Bottom half of the corner at the wall juncture by the handsink in the packaging area has not been properly sealed. Seal the wall juncture.

B) Wall covering next to wrapping station was loose in the packaging area. Repair the wall and reattach the covering.

C) Walls and doorway to the indoor walkin freezer are not properly sealed. Wood, spray foam, and insulation are exposed. Properly seal the walls and doorway at the walkin freezer.

D) Dust accumulation was observed in the walkin cooler on the condenser. Clean all the general surfaces of the walls and ceiling in the walkin cooler as needed, and maintain them clean.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - A number of foods that are received at the facility arrive in bulk, and the store repackages the products into smaller bagged and/or cryovaced portions. Items require safe food handling instructions on individual packages and bags. Some items were observed without labels during inspection. Owner was advised to provide proper labels on all smaller portions. (see general comments)

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750.140c - Thermostat was observed at 50F in the 3 door freezer containing cabbage pork steamed buns, fish and various other frozen foods. Inspector's infrared registered temperatures ranging as follows from the top shelf to the bottom shelf in the freezer: 49F/50F; 40F; 23F; 13F; -1F. Foods on the top shelf of the freezer had surface temperatures ranging from 47F to 50F+ and were starting to thaw. An internal temperature of cabbage pork buns on the top shelf was at 35F-40F. Surface temperatures for products on the next shelf down were in the 30 degree range and were still firm to the touch. All other foods on subsequent lower shelves were still frozen solid and had surface temperatures from the high 20 degree range to 0 degrees Fahrenheit. Owner moved all products out of the freezer in question per the request of inspector. Foods were either placed in the other available reach-in freezers in the store or in the walkin freezer. 
Owner stated he will make a call for service to get the freezer repaired. Owner was given inspector's business card and will call for a spot check on the freezer once it is repaired. Freezer in question will not be used until it is properly repaired and able to maintain frozen foods frozen. 

Stored frozen foods shall be maintained frozen.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Several boxes of various products were observed on the floor. Owner noted a deliver was received late on Thursday. Owner was advised boxes containing foods, rice paper, etc. need to be stored at least 6 inches off the floor until items are able to be stocked on shelves.

Food shall be protected at all times and stored at least 6 inches off the floor. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee preparing to repackage pork bung washed hands without proper technique. Paper towels were not available to properly dry hands and be used as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employee properly washed hands once paper towels were available.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Glass door chest freezers and coolers were observed with varying degrees of ice accumulation. Defrost units as needed to minimize ice accumulation and allow for ease in cleaning.

B) Soiled butcher style paper was observed lining shelving on the left side of the display cooler used for storage of potentially hazardous foods. Remove the soiled paper liner and cease the practice of using absorbent material for lining shelving in the display cooler.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Facility did not have chlorine test kit for checking concentration of bleach solutions. A set of test strips were provided by inspector. Owner and employee that helps repackage bulk foods were advised on use of strips and proper concentrations of bleach solutions for ware washing at the 3 part sink versus wiping down general surfaces (i.e. handles of coolers & freezers, etc.).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) bottom inside 2 door freezer (baby clam meat freezer - splash/buildup);  and
B) tracks of glass door chest freezers and coolers (debris accumulation).

Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Small Styrofoam trays were observed in the 3rd compartment of the 3 part sink. Some trays had varying amounts of soil accumulation due to location and level of debris accumulation in the compartment of the sink. Trays were removed from the sink, and several of the trays were discarded. Proper storage of single service items was discussed.

Single service articles shall be stored in a manner that protects items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - A) Paper towels were not available at the handsink in the packaging area. Paper towels were provided.

B) Handsink in restroom was soiled with grimy buildup. Clean the handsinks and related fixtures daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

C) Restroom door self-closer was loose, and the restroom door was not shutting properly. Repair the restroom door so it is self-closing.

Maintain a supply of soap and paper towels at all handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Maintain handsinks and related fixtures clean and in good repair.
All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220. - The walkin cooler floor was soiled under shelving, especially under the storage palettes. Clean the walkin cooler floor.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1210 & 1220 - A) Bottom half of the corner at the wall juncture by the handsink in the packaging area remained to be sealed. Finish sealing the wall juncture.

B) Dust accumulation was observed in the walkin cooler on the condenser, the ceiling, and on the wall around the door by the thermostat. Clean all the general surfaces of the walls and ceiling in the walkin cooler.

Walls and ceilings must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
750-100 REPEAT: Cut jack fruit is observed on display on the front counter. Fruit appears dull and dry. Discarded and temped at ambient temperature (80F). In addition to the unrefrigerated nature of the food, the facility does not have the necessary plumbing to properly handle the cutting of produce and other foods. Cease cutting produce until a proper three compartment sink and food preparation area can be installed. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

750-100 A number of the glass jars of kim chee are observed with opened lids. Product had spilled from the bottles and was spilling onto a baking sheet beneath the foods. Also, a number of plastic wrapped silken tofu is observed with an expiration date of July 24, 2016. These packages were also observed bulging. Finally, a container of lily bulbs was discarded due to being under pressure and bloated.  Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-250  REPEAT: The two large open air display coolers in the frozen foods room are observed holding foods at temperatures from 41F up to 71F. A number of foods were discarded (see the Order of Destruction). Foods were all stocked on the previous day. A small amount of foods were observed to indicate 'Refrigerate After Opening' on the label. These foods were allowed to stay in the cooler. Another small portion of foods on the top shelf and the lowest shelf were probed and found to be at 41F or under. These items were also allowed to be kept. There is a thick frost accumulation on the lower shelf of the tofu display cooler. The air is obviously not moving through the unit properly. DO NOT PLACE ANY FOOD INTO THIS DISPLAY COOLER UNTIL IT IS SERVICED. The second display cooler primarily houses whole, intact produce. Continue using this cooler for whole produce only. Cease storing cut melons and foods requiring refrigeration in this cooler. All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-260 Observed the large display cooler to be holding temperatures from 41F to 71F. See violation 3a and the Order of Destruction. Cease storing food in this cooler until the unit can be serviced. Enough hot or cold storage units used for displaying potentially hazardous foods shall be provided to maintain proper product temperature requirements.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed various uncovered pieces of frozen meats in the reach-in freezer. Make sure that packages are wrapped securely so the contents do not fall out.  Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed the new wooden shelving to be constructed of unfinished wood. Seal the wood. Also, observed the reach-in freezers to be coated with a thick accumulation of frost. Defrost the reach-in freezers.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: 750-820a The facility does not have a proper three compartment sink. Should Little World Mart continue to cut produce and repackage they will need a specific area designated for the washing, rinsing, and sanitizing of utensils. A three compartment sink should be provided for this purpose. For manual washing, rinsing and sanitizing of utensils and equipment, a sink with no fewer then three compartments shall be provided and used..

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g A test kit of chlorine test strips should be available for testing created buckets and sinks of bleach water. Provide bleach test strips. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-800c The facility does not have a three compartment sink available for wash, rinse and santizing. Utensils used for the cutting of produce and meats are not being sanitized. Provide a three compartment sink or cease cutting produce and repackaging meats.  Utensils should be sanitized in 50ppm Cl for at least 60 seconds. Where equipment and utensils are used for the preparation of  potentially hazardous foods on a continuous or production-line basis, utensils and the food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized at intervals throughout the day on a schedule subject to the approval of the regulatory authority.  This schedule shall be based on food temperature, type of food, and amount of food particle accumulation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The gap of the plastic edging pieces of the display coolers is observed soiled with accumulated food crumbs. Clean the display cooler shelves. Also, the reach-in freezers are observed soiled with various pieces of meat, fish, and crustacean parts. Clean the reach-in freezers. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(a) Observed the facility to not have a handsink in the food preparation area. Provide a handsink in your food preparation location.  Lavatories shall be at least the number required by law, shall be installed according to law and shall be located to permit convenient use by all employees in food preparation areas and utensil washing areas.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Flooring under all food preparation surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Place tile on the floor where food preparation is to occur. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 the ceiling is constructed of acoustic tiles. Provide a smooth and cleanable surface over the area where food preparation is to occur.  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 Observed the facility to be operating as a Medium Risk Establishment. The facility may choose to upgrade to this classification and will then require a certified food manager. Or, the facility may choose to cease cutting produce and repackaging meat. If they cease these activities then they may stay a Retail Class C (which won't require the three compartment sink, handsink, or certified food manager. All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: 750-100 Observed two containers of Spiced Jumbo Thick Dry Tofu (21 oz) to be leaking and spoiled. Items were pulled from cooler during the inspection and discarded.  There were also two containers of Quail Eggs with past expiration dates= pulled from use during inspection. Finally, a wrapped baked good labeled Rice Cake was observed firm and growing mold spores along the top. Discarded during the inspection. This particular cake was stored in the reach-in cooler. Other fresh cakes were observed stored on the counters. They were soft to the touch. A Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-110g Multiple foods are observed with proper labeling requirements. A number of frozen meats and fresh fish did not have a proper label. Owner expressed concern over the lack of labeling and acknowledged that many foods were sliced and  packaged today. Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name;, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-250 Observed the two open air display coolers to be  holding  temepratures over 41F. The second of the coolers is holding temperature at 58-62F and foods at 58F. Embargo forms were completed to check on the refrigeration requirements of the foods being held in this cooler. Most of these items were stocked around noon. Each food had the label read and the time of stock checked. Foods stocked around noon were allowed to be put into the adjacent cooler. The second cooler is definitely not holdinng proper temperature and is going to be used to hold whole produce and non-refrigerated items. This second cooler was just stocked between midnight and noon today. Many of the foods contained in this cooler were tofu products stocked between noon and 1:00pm. Defrost cycles and overloading of the unit was discussed. Melon, kim chee, and tofus  were all probed
The first cooler has various temperatures between the various shelves. A shelf found to be holding foods at 40F is going to be used to hold the cold foods moved from cooler #2. Cut melon observed at 48F (probed) in the first cooler was discarded.  All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment: 750-260 There are two open air display coolers present in the back room. One of the coolers is holding temperatures in the high 50s to low 60s. The other cooler has shelves that are inconsistent. Temperature in cooler #1 ranges from 39-48F. Coolers will be checked next Monday. Embargo information will be checked next Monday.  Enough hot or cold storage units used for displaying potentially hazardous foods shall be provided to maintain proper product temperature requirements.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140(a)  The open air refrigerators have improperly placed thermometers. The second cooler has a thermometer that is not accurately reading the air temperature. The additional thermometer in the second cooler is located far in the back and is not easily read. The first cooler and second cooler need to have thermometers that are located so they are easily read. All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed frozen shrimp and whole duck thawing at room temperature. Foods were still observed under 40F. Cease thawing at room temperature. Thaw in cooler.  Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-130(b) Observed boxes of foods stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler and aisles. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed shelled nuts to be stored with a bowl as a service utensils. Cease using a bowl for serving. Use a scoop with a proper handle that extends out of food. Minimize hand contact with nuts. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed cardboard on the pallets of the back storage room and on the aisle shelves. Cease use of soiled cardboard.
